prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a continuous bright foreground masonry ledge at the bottom of the frame roughly 0.3 to 0.8 metres from the camera wearer, receding along a flat wall surface toward a mid-ground worker in a white-blue shirt at roughly 2 to 3 metres and a second worker in a pink shirt further to the right at roughly 3.5 to 5 metres (about 1.5 to 2 metres behind the first worker). Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's hand enters at the bottom within arm's reach (under 0.5 metres) to place a fourth brick onto the three-brick stack on the lower left, while in frame 5 a vertical scaffolding pole enters the far-left foreground at roughly 0.5 metres, partially occluding the background. Simultaneously, the nearer worker leans slightly closer to the wall ledge and extends his left arm downward to place a brick within his own arm's reach, while the farther worker behind the scaffolding poles also reaches down toward the wall surface in frames 4 and 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground brick stack, the wooden scaffolding poles, and the stepped depth planes of the two workers from the similarly coloured plaster and sky background. However, the depth map is unreliable in the upper-left and upper-right background, where the distant wall above the scaffolding and the bright sky both collapse into uniform black (infinite depth) and thin scaffolding bars lose sharp depth boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the nearer worker in the upper-left/centre as a pink 'person' mask (roughly 2 to 3 metres away, positioned above and to the left of the foreground ledge) across all 5 frames, as he leans over the brick course and reaches down with his left hand while turning his head slightly toward the camera wearer by frame 5. It also detects the farther worker (roughly 3.5 to 5 metres away, to the right of the nearer worker and partly occluded by scaffolding poles) only in frame 3 as a fragmented brown 'person' mask, and detects the camera wearer's own right hand and forearm entering at the bottom foreground (within 0.5 metres, reaching the lower-left brick stack) as a 'person' mask only in frame 5. The map makes it easy to track the silhouette change of the nearer worker's torso and extended left arm in frame 5 against the cluttered scaffolding background that blends with his clothing in RGB. However, the segmentation map is highly unreliable for the scene as a whole: it completely misses the farther worker in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, misses the camera wearer's foreground hand in frames 3 and 4, and fails to segment any of the bricks, masonry walls, or scaffolding poles that define the physical layout and occlusions.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders a single yellow body skeleton for the nearer worker in the upper-left/centre (about 2 to 3 metres from the camera wearer), capturing his sideways-leaning torso, his right arm braced to the left, and his head keypoints oriented downward toward the brick ledge in frames 1 to 4 before tilting slightly toward the camera wearer in frame 5. Across frames 3 to 5, the skeleton clearly tracks his left arm extending downward toward the masonry ledge to place a brick within his arm's reach, then bracing against the ledge as his shoulders arch upward in frame 5. Compared to the RGB strip, the skeleton lines make the articulation of his shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints immediately distinct despite the sideways camera orientation and clutter of scaffolding poles behind him. However, the pose map is unreliable everywhere else: it completely fails to detect the second worker 1.5 to 2 metres further back on the right, misses the camera wearer's own foreground hand manipulating the bricks within 0.5 metres in frames 3 to 5, omits all lower-body keypoints occluded behind the masonry ledge, and produces no magenta hand skeletons in any frame.
